Title: Dynamic Modeling of Microalgae Growth and Lipid Production under Transient Light and Nitrogen Conditions

Abstract: ABSTRACT: We developed a new dynamic model to characterize how light and nitrogen regulate the cellular processes of photosynthetic microalgae leading to transient changes in the production of neutral lipids, carbohydrates, and biomass. Our model recapitulated the versatile neutral lipid synthesis pathways via (i) carbon reuse from carbohydrate metabolism under nitrogen sufficiency and (ii) fixed carbon redirection under nitrogen depletion. We also characterized the effects of light adaptation, light inhibition hysteresis, and nitrogen limitation on photosynthetic carbon fixation. Model: Dynamic microalgae growth and lipid production model
Laws:
(9) [constitutive] Optical absorbance per unit length from the contributions of chlorophyll and the remaining biomass carbon.
(10) [constitutive] Average attenuated light intensity over the reactor’s optical path.
(11) [constitutive] Average reference light intensity over the optical path without biomass attenuation.
(12) [constitutive] Photosynthetic carbon-fixation rate per functional biomass, with a Steele-type response to average light intensity.
(13) [constitutive] Light saturation intensity in the carbon-fixation law, determined from biomass, photosynthetic capacity, chlorophyll, and adjusted carbon yield on light energy.
(14) [constitutive] Carbon yield on light energy adjusted downward as reference light intensity increases.
(15) [constitutive] Nitrate-dependent fraction of carbon redirected from carbohydrate toward neutral-lipid accumulation, increasing as nitrate becomes scarce.
(16) [constitutive] Chlorophyll-a degradation rate modulated by nitrate availability and reference light intensity, representing degradation under nitrogen starvation and high-light stress.
(17) [constitutive] Computes nitrate uptake as a nitrate-concentration-scaled rate whose maximum is regulated by the cellular nitrogen quota.
(18) [definition] Defines the total cellular nitrogen quota as intracellular nitrogen concentration divided by total biomass carbon concentration.
(1) [balance] Balances functional biomass carbon through photosynthetic production and functional biomass degradation.
(2) [balance] Balances carbohydrate carbon through carbon allocation, respiration, nitrogen-uptake-associated consumption, and redirection to lipids.
(3) [balance] Balances neutral-lipid carbon through nitrogen-uptake-associated synthesis and carbon redirected from carbohydrate accumulation.
(4) [balance] Balances chlorophyll-a carbon through light-regulated synthesis associated with nitrogen uptake and chlorophyll degradation.
(5) [balance] Computes the decline in reactor nitrate concentration due to nitrate uptake.
(6) [balance] Computes intracellular nitrogen accumulation with the sign opposite to the nitrate uptake rate.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- X_{cd}: Concentration of functional biomass (algal biomass excluding carbohydrates and neutral lipids) as C
- X_{carb}: Concentration of carbohydrates as C
- X_{nl}: Concentration of neutral lipids as C
- X_{chl}: Concentration of Chl-a as C
- S_{NO3}: Concentration of nitrate as N in the reactor
- X_{N}: Concentration of cellular nitrogen as N

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- X_{C}: Total biomass carbon concentration
- S_{NO3_0}: Initial extracellular nitrate concentration

Model-wide assumptions:
- Optical cross‑section parameters a and b are taken as constant regardless of cultivation conditions.
- The composition of functional biomass is fixed to CH1.8O0.5N0.2.
- Nitrate uptake is assumed to equal the nitrate removed from the medium.

answer.description: The model describes Dunaliella viridis growth and production of biomass, carbohydrates, and neutral lipids in a photobioreactor under changing light and nitrogen conditions. It predicts the dynamics of these cellular carbon pools, chlorophyll, extracellular nitrate, and cellular nitrogen using light attenuation and photosynthetic fixation, quota-regulated nitrate uptake, nitrogen-dependent carbon allocation to lipids, and chlorophyll dynamics.
